title: Poland's jazz competition and the young trumpeter
summary: He plays and then judges a week-long Warsaw competition, impressed by a band whose trumpeter hits notes only dogs could hear.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yeah - and then, of course you know I played Poland and I loved the band in Poland - I went there to play a thing called the, uh, jazz party of some kind and it's a competition thing - they have hundreds of Polish bands - you wouldn't believe it - for seven days - hundreds of them just appearing one after the other. All kinds of bands and singers and dancers - oh, God - everything.
And, this is in Warsaw you say--
And, I did two records there; I was there twice; once as a musician and the second time I went as a judge of that thing that was happening and I played too.

Because the band I was with had won the competition the year before and I must say, they call themselves The Old Timers and I don't know why they only call themselves The Old Timers, the oldest guy in the band is about 24. But, anyway, they had a trumpet player - I don't know what the hell he wanted me in the band for -- I never heard such a trumpet player in my life; he does everything--

Oh - boy - never heard anything like this guy; he hit notes so high on his horn that only dogs could hear--- I mean, and really play. Well, I understand that he plays in the symphony orchestra - first chair in the symphony orchestra and he plays with their big radio orchestra there and that's a big band; playing Ellington style music - or that big band style-- then, he has this jazz band.
So you see, they had a late start--
I don't suppose you remember his name - do you?

No, not off-hand - no. But, you see, they got a late start with their jazz; you know, it wasn't easy like for me and for Americans that heard it forbidden to play in there too-- and it was / - the Nazi took over - bang - nothing; then--now the Russians but anyway, I couldn't believe my ears-- when I was a judge on this thing when I had to sit and listen to all these bands; you can't believe it.

Because of that, well, I just told you - of the fact that he got such a late start-- I even heard gospel singers-- you know, singing the early gospel songs of America - isn't that something. You wonder where the hell they got it from--
